## Class

**217 backslashed-path occurrences** in job `100874330553`. The clearest specimen:

```
assert 'src/rebar/live.py:1' in 'criteria vocabulary check failed:\nsrc\rebar\live.py:1: deprecated vocabula…'
```

This is NOT merely a test-assertion problem. rebar emits repo-relative paths into **user- and
machine-facing artifacts** — criteria-vocabulary diagnostics, review findings, file-impact entries,
commit-trailer scans — and those paths are consumed as strings and compared against forward-slash
forms. On Windows they render with `\`, so the artifact itself differs by platform.

## What the fix must decide

Repo-relative paths in rebar's **output** should be normalised to forward slashes at the rendering
boundary — the same convention git itself uses — rather than each assertion being taught to accept
both. Fixing this in the assertions would leave the real artifact platform-dependent, which is the
defect. Locate the rendering boundaries (the diagnostic formatters, the file-impact writer, the
review-finding serialiser) and normalise there.

Note this class was **not** in the bug's original class list; it was found by re-reading the log for
this decomposition. It is the largest non-`lock.py` class by raw occurrence count.

## Blocked by S1

## Proving command

```
uv run --no-sync pytest tests/unit/test_cli_body_guard.py tests/unit/test_code_review_artifact.py \
  tests/unit/test_pai_output.py -p no:cacheprovider -q
```
on `windows-latest`, plus a cross-platform artifact-equality proof: a test that renders a
repo-relative path and asserts the rendered form contains `/` and no `\`, so it fails on Windows if
the normalisation is removed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Repo-relative paths in rebar's rendered output use `/` on every platform.
2. The normalisation is enforced by a test that would fail on Windows if reverted, not only by the
   incidental passing of consumers.
